absent: Security mediation for exec credentials, trace and perf side effects, and full binprm allocation and teardown are not shown.
User namespace privilege evaluation, id mapping, and mount propagation beyond membership checks are not shown.
Descriptor table growth, file reference state details, driver flush contracts, and dnotify behaviour are not shown.
Lease manager callbacks, deadlock detector internals, global blocked table sizing, and lock cache setup are not shown.
Signal table cache setup, task list exclusion scope beyond replacement, and interval timer internals are not shown.

findings.text: Exec, mount, and file helpers usable from other translation units include task naming, dumpability marking, mount suid checks, close on exec sweep, file flush and close, and reference release.
POSIX lock helpers usable from other translation units include close-time removal, generic dispatch, inode processing, record allocation and release, conflock copying, and waiter wakeup.

Exec identity, credential, and dumpability processing operates on binprm and file state, selecting identity source, deriving set-id credentials with security mediation, and adjusting dumpability and namespace ancestry when readability fails.

Signal handler sharing is resolved by installing a private table when the reference count shows sharing. The replacement starts singly referenced, inherits existing actions under exclusion, becomes visible to the task, and the prior table reference is released. Exclusive tables need no change and allocation failure signals memory exhaustion.
Task naming truncates input to leave room for termination, notifies rename and perf observers, copies the retained prefix, and clears the remainder of the fixed comm store.
Transparent interpreter execution attributes identity to the outer executable, while ordinary execution attributes identity to the executed file itself.
Exec timer handling removes CPU timers while holding signal exclusion, then exits interval timers and clears pending interval signals for the execing task.
Unreadable executables force nondumpable marking and re-anchor the binprm user namespace to the nearest ancestor privileged over the file, moving namespace references accordingly.

Set-id credential handling ignores suid and sgid on nosuid mounts, under no-new-privs, without set bits, without later execute permission, or without namespace mappings. Otherwise set-user updates the effective user and set-group with group execute updates the effective group, each marking personality state for clearing on set-id.
Suid trust requires absence of nosuid, membership in the same mount namespace as current, and containment of the filesystem user namespace. Mounts from other namespaces never confer suid trust.
Inode mode and identity inspection for exec uses write exclusion on the inode semaphore, acquired before rechecking mode and mapped ids and released before acting on the result.

Close on exec clears marked descriptors in ascending order, detaching each file from the table and updating open and full hints plus the next-free hint. Actual closes happen outside files exclusion with scheduling opportunities, then scanning resumes.

File close combines flush with reference drop. Flush reports success on corrupt zero counts, runs optional driver flush, and for non-path files also handles dnotify and POSIX unlock for the closer. Final close reference triggers deferred destruction, with a fast single-reference path and generic fallback.

Close-time POSIX cleanup does nothing without POSIX state on the inode. Otherwise it requests whole-file unlock for the closing owner on the closing file and afterwards releases driver private data when present.
File lock requests use filesystem-specific handling when offered, otherwise generic POSIX handling on the file inode.

POSIX lock requests move among conflict check, queue-or-fail, query-only return, and owner-range update. Conflicts fail fast when nonblocking, queue when sleeping unless deadlock is detected, queries return status without mutation, same-type overlaps merge, differing types replace, trim, split, or delete, and affected waiters are awakened while unused records are freed.

Inode lock context appears on first non-unlock use, starts with empty flock, POSIX, and lease queues, and only one allocation wins installation while losers are freed. Unlock-only paths never create context.

Lock records are zeroed with initialized queue linkage at allocation and may be freed only after wait queues are idle, list and hash membership is empty, and driver plus lease-manager references are detached. Dispose lists are drained by unlinking each member before freeing.
POSIX ownership compares stored owner pointers for equality, blocked indexing derives from the owner pointer value, and core headers convert to enclosing records through container linkage.

Conflock copying transfers owner, process, flags, type, range, and lease-manager hooks without file or driver linkage, while full copying adds file association and driver linkage with driver copy notification. Replacement records inherit the full waiter queue with each waiter reparented.

Blocked waiters attach beneath the deepest conflicting waiter, inherit global indexing for POSIX types, and on wakeup detach from global and local queues, route through lease-manager notification when available otherwise wait-queue wakeup, and mark completion with ordered blocker clearing. Trimmed survivors also wake their own waiters, and fresh records join the inode queue ahead of a cursor.

POSIX inode mutation holds a file read guard together with the inode context spinlock. Global blocked exclusion is taken only around waiter insertion, transfer, wakeup, and deadlock checks, with an early exit when no waiters exist. Expirable lease callbacks run after dropping both guards, then the operation restarts.
Signal table copying nests the old table spinlock inside interrupt-disabled task-list write exclusion, covering action copying and publication.
Close-on-exec scanning holds files spinlock while examining and detaching descriptors, dropping it for each close and reschedule and reacquiring before continuing, with final release at end of table.
Lock-context installation serializes on the inode spinlock with acquire-release pairing to publication, while exec CPU-timer exit serializes on the signal spinlock with interrupts disabled.

A POSIX lock record pairs a core header carrying linkage, wait queues, blocked membership, owner, file, type, flags, and blocker link with range endpoints and optional driver plus lease-manager hooks. Context state groups flock, POSIX, and lease queues under one spinlock.

Range edge handling must not increment the maximum offset, so adjacency uses decremented starts. Lease expiration requires dropping guards before invoking callbacks to avoid deadlock, then retry. Flush must not proceed when the reference count is already zero.
Whole-file unlock-all uses start zero through maximum offset with unlock type and POSIX plus close disposition.
Descriptor tables advance close-on-exec scans by machine-word-sized groups, with per-word full hints and a next-free hint maintained on clear.
